name: Body shaving / hair removal for skin texture

image.caption: " 12 - ITALY - cosmetics of italian brands - Hair and skin care, scrub (gommage) shaving soap, body lotions and deodorant

lead: Men shave or remove chest, arm, leg or back hair to look smoother and to show muscle definition more clearly, especially for physique photos and competitions. The change is visible immediately.
It is a style practice in appearance communities rather than a medical treatment, and little research addresses it for skin texture specifically.

paras: Razors or trimmers cut hair at the skin surface, so the look is temporary and repeated as hair grows back. Men most often shave facial hair, and some extend it to the chest, abdomen, underarms and legs.

Cuts, razor burn, razor bumps and ingrown hairs are reported. One well-known investigation of an MRSA skin infection outbreak on a college football team identified cosmetic body shaving and turf burns as facilitating factors.

angle.text: Shaving the chest, arms, legs or back gives a smoother look and shows muscle definition more clearly, especially for physique photos and competitions. The result is visible straight away and is treated as a style choice.

lead: Body shaving and hair removal, in this context, means removing chest, arm, leg or back hair to make skin look smoother or to show muscle definition. It is discussed in appearance communities as a style practice rather than a medical treatment. Men most often shave facial hair, and some also shave the chest, abdomen, underarms, legs or pubic area [1].

Published research on cosmetic body shaving is limited. One well-known investigation described an outbreak of MRSA skin infections among players on a college football team in which cosmetic body shaving and turf burns were identified as facilitating factors [2].
infobox: Cuts, razor burn, razor bumps, ingrown hairs

paras: Methods include wet shaving with a straight or safety razor, electric shaving and trimmers [1]. Wikipedia notes shaving history from copper razors around 3000 BC to disposable razors popularized after 1974 [1].

Reported effects include cuts, razor burn, razor bumps (pseudofolliculitis barbae) and ingrown hairs [1]. Wikipedia states that shaving does not cause terminal hair to grow back thicker, coarser or darker, and attributes the impression to the blunt tip of cut hair [1].

No studies found on body shaving specifically for skin texture. A retrospective cohort study of a 2003 college football team investigated an MRSA outbreak of cellulitis and abscesses among 100 players and linked cosmetic body shaving and turf burns to its spread [2].
